Learning happens
in the conversation.

Students need time to question, try, reconsider, and try again. Our lessons make room for all of it.

“What makes you think that?”A small question that takes thinking further.

    Start with a clear purpose.

    Know what you’re learning, why it matters, and what success looks like.

    Put your thinking into words.

  4. 04

    Use feedback to move forward.

    Recognize what worked, revise with intention, and take one meaningful next step.

A TEACHER FIRST

Hi, I’m Matthew.

I founded Ink Wire Education to give students space to think deeply, ask good questions, and develop their own voice.

My background includes ten years in international schools, including YK Pao School in Shanghai and an IB PYP school. I bring that classroom experience to online lessons that combine high expectations with thoughtful support.

Master of EducationOntario-certified teacherInternational-school experience

A good lesson should leave a student with a stronger skill—and something new to wonder about.

GOOD QUESTIONS

A few things
you might be wondering.

Choosing support for your child should feel clear and personal.

Who are the classes for?

Ink Wire works with students in Grades 3–12, including learners in bilingual and international schools. The reading level, language support, and writing expectations are matched to the learner.

How do the online lessons work?

Live lessons take place on Zoom and combine discussion, reading, and writing. Reading and practice between lessons help students arrive prepared. The format and lesson length are agreed around the student’s needs.

Can you support our school curriculum?

Support can be aligned with IB, Cambridge and British curricula, Common Core, and Canadian expectations, including literary analysis and exam-oriented writing. Share the student’s grade, course, and current goals so we can discuss the right fit.

Does my child need to be a confident reader already?

No. A starting conversation helps identify the right level of challenge and support. We can work on reading confidence, English-language development, or more advanced analysis and writing.

How will I know how my child is progressing?

Clear learning goals, student work, and teacher feedback make progress visible. The new Learning Studio prototype also demonstrates how parent summaries and next steps could be brought together in one place.

How do we get started?

Tell Matthew about the student’s grade, interests, and goals using the enquiry below. You can then discuss an appropriate program, availability, and pricing before making a commitment.
